title: JEV vs. LLMs as Rubric Judges: Cheaper, Faster, and Wrong in the Same Places
abstract: LLM judges score outputs against rubrics well enough to have become the norm, both in benchmarks and as rewards for training. Jev, a classifier-like alternative its creators call a "decision model", returns probabilities over permitted answers with a calibrated confidence score, which LLM judges do not natively provide. We compare Jev with three flash-tier LLM judges on nine panels from seven benchmarks with human judgments, giving every judge identical criterion texts. The LLM judges run in two setups: holistically, reading a whole rubric at once as Jev does, and one criterion at a time. Jev can often stand in for them. They cost 16 to 325 times as much and take 28 to 350 times as long, yet in each setup Jev's accuracy differs significantly from theirs in at most 8 of 27 paired comparisons, ahead mostly on binary checklist criteria and behind only on ordinal ones. Despite their different designs, the two kinds of judge err alike. On ordinal criteria, all LLM judges and Jev depart from the human raters together, agreeing more with one another than with the labels and mostly assigning lower levels. On Jev's most confident errors, about 96% of LLM verdicts repeat its wrong answer, where independent errors would give about half. Intuitively, calibrated confidence should make Jev an ideal first stage of a cascade that defers uncertain verdicts to an LLM judge. Yet such cascades only lower cost while adding little accuracy: even with oracle thresholds, none beats the best single judge by more than 2.7 points. Calibration can tell a cascade when to defer, but the cascade also needs a fallback that errs elsewhere; these judges are wrong in the same places. These findings, which hold in both setups and at high reasoning effort, suggest that a cascade of judges succeeds only when its judges make complementary errors, and that future decision models should be designed afresh with that aim.

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: In our hypothetical graduate seminar on Evaluation Methods for Language Models, today’s lecture is on Jev as a typed classifier for rubric judging. Recent work such as “JEV-as-a-Judge: Accept When Confident, Escalate When Unsure” explores confidence-based escalation, while “Evaluating Judges as Evaluators: The JETTS Benchmark of LLM-as-Judges as Test-Time Scaling Evaluators” studies judge behavior in evaluation pipelines. The field is looking for reliable ways to scale evaluation; this paper asks whether structured, batched decisions can reduce the cost of rubric grading. Yes, Noah?
segments.zh: 在我们假设的研究生课程“语言模型评估方法”上，今天的讲座讲的是把Jev当作带类型的分类器来做评分标准评判。最近的工作，比如《JEV-as-a-Judge: Accept When Confident, Escalate When Unsure》，探讨的是基于置信度的升级机制；而《Evaluating Judges as Evaluators: The JETTS Benchmark of LLM-as-Judges as Test-Time Scaling Evaluators》则研究评判者在评估流程中的行为。这个领域正在寻找可靠的方法来扩展评估规模；这篇论文问的是，结构化、批量的决策能否降低评分标准打分的成本。是的，Noah？

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Hi Professor, is Jev generating explanations, or does it answer in a more constrained format?
segments.zh: 教授您好，Jev是会生成解释，还是以更受限的格式来回答？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: It gives fixed-choice answers with probabilities over allowed verdicts, rather than composing a free-form explanation for each criterion. The practical difference is the unit of work. A conventional L-L-M judge is called once for every submission–criterion pair. Jev can receive one submission and all its criteria together, then return structured verdicts and confidence scores. That makes it a plausible lower-cost first-stage grader, but the important question is whether its accuracy holds up across different kinds of criteria.
segments.zh: 它给出的是固定选项的答案，并附带各个允许判定结果的概率，而不是针对每条标准自由组织一段解释。实际差别在于工作单元不同。传统的LLM评审是每对提交和标准调用一次。Jev可以一次接收一份提交及其所有标准，然后返回结构化的判定和置信度分数。这让它有望成为一种成本更低的第一阶段评分器，但关键问题是它的准确率能否在不同类型的标准上都站得住脚。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: So it can bundle criteria, but does the study compare the same grading tasks and inputs?
segments.zh: 所以它确实能把多个标准打包处理，但这项研究比较的是相同的评分任务和输入吗？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: The comparison covers 5,003 submission–criterion pairs in 9 panels drawn from 7 public benchmarks. Jev is compared with three flash-tier L-L-M judges: Luna, Gemini, and DeepSeek. The criteria come from rubrics fixed before the study, but the complete prompts and input conditions were not identical. Two panels contain only binary criteria; the other 7 are graded panels, some of which also include binary criteria. That distinction matters because performance differed by criterion type.
segments.zh: 这项比较覆盖了来自7个公开基准的9个评审组、共5003个提交-评分标准对。Jev与三个flash级别的LLM评审员进行了对比：Luna、Gemini和DeepSeek。评分标准来自研究前就固定好的评分细则，但完整的提示词和输入条件并不完全相同。其中两个评审组只包含二元评分标准，另外7个是分级评审组，部分也包含二元标准。这一区分很重要，因为不同标准类型下的表现存在差异。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: For binary criteria, verdict accuracy is the share of predictions matching the label. For graded criteria, exact accuracy requires the predicted level to match the label exactly; the study also reports quadratic-weighted kappa, which measures ordinal agreement. In a representative binary task, RiceChem, Jev Choice reached 81% verdict accuracy on 819 pairs, while the L-L-M judges ranged from 76.1% to 79.2%. Jev’s advantages were mostly on binary criteria, whereas its graded results were less competitive.
segments.zh: 对于二元标准，判定准确率就是预测结果与标签一致的占比。对于分级标准，精确准确率要求预测的等级与标签完全一致；研究还报告了二次加权kappa，用来衡量有序一致性。在一个有代表性的二元任务RiceChem中，Jev Choice在819对样本上达到了81%的判定准确率，而大语言模型评委的准确率在76.1%到79.2%之间。Jev的优势主要体现在二元标准上，而在分级标准上的表现就没那么有竞争力了。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Quick question: when the paper says results are inconclusive, does that mean the systems are effectively tied?
segments.zh: 快速问一下：论文说结果不确定，是不是就意味着这些系统实际上打平了？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: No. The authors resampled units 10,000 times and treated a comparison as separated when its 95% interval excluded zero. They also tested parity using a five-point margin chosen after verdict collection. A result that establishes neither separation nor parity is simply inconclusive; it does not demonstrate equivalence. Across 27 paired accuracy comparisons, 8 were separated before correction, and most of the rest were inconclusive. So we should not summarize the findings as Jev matching L-L-M judges overall.
segments.zh: 不是。作者对单元做了1万次重采样，并把95%区间不包含零的比较视为有显著差异。他们还用了一个在收集完判定结果之后才选定的五分边际来检验等效性。一个既不能确立差异、也不能确立等效的结果，就是单纯没有定论；它并不证明两者等价。在27组配对准确率比较中，有8组在校正前显示出差异，其余大多数都没有定论。所以我们不能把这些发现总结成Jev整体上与L-L-M评审相当。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: The cost and elapsed-time measurements show the operational attraction, with important boundaries. Across the 9 panels, Jev Choice cost $0.063, compared with $20.587 for Gemini, or 325 times as much. Recorded wall time was 29 seconds for Jev and 950 seconds for Gemini, about 33 times as long. These numbers reflect the study’s call structure, prices, API conditions, and concurrency; they are not evidence of token or compute savings, nor a normalized latency comparison.
segments.zh: 成本和耗时数据说明了它在实际运行上的吸引力，但也有一些重要边界。在9个评审组中，Jev Choice花费0.063美元，而Gemini花费20.587美元，是前者的325倍。记录的墙钟时间方面，Jev为29秒，Gemini为950秒，大约是前者的33倍。这些数字反映的是该研究的调用结构、价格、API条件和并发情况，并不能证明节省了token或算力，也不是归一化的延迟比较。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Hold on, why can judges agree with one another yet still disagree with human labels?
segments.zh: 等等，为什么评判者之间能达成一致，却仍然和人工标注不一致呢？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: On every graded panel, the matched judges’ average agreement with one another exceeded their average agreement with human labels. Yet on 6 of 7 graded panels, every matched judge predicted a lower mean level than the labels. Agreement measures whether ratings move together, not whether they land at the same point on the scale. On ELLIPSE learner essays, for example, Gemini’s exact accuracy was 29.8%, while Jev Choice’s average prediction sat 1.25 levels below the label mean.
segments.zh: 在每一个评分小组中，配对评委彼此之间的平均一致度都高于他们与人工标注之间的平均一致度。然而在7个评分小组中的6个里，每个配对评委预测的平均等级都低于标注。一致度衡量的是评分是否同向变动，而不是它们是否落在量表上的同一点。以ELLIPSE学习者作文为例，Gemini的精确准确率为29.8%，而Jev Choice的平均预测比标注均值低了1.25个等级。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: A post-hoc analysis shifted Jev Choice’s ELLIPSE predictions upward by one level; exact accuracy rose from 13.4% to 50.4%, near the 51.4% rater reference. That reference scores each rater against the mean of the other raters, so it is not a ceiling for an automated judge. The shift suggests that scale location contributes to the observed mismatch, but it was not a prospective correction and does not identify its cause. Missing conventions are one possibility among several, not a demonstrated explanation.
segments.zh: 事后分析把Jev Choice在ELLIPSE上的预测整体上调了一级，精确准确率从13.4%升到50.4%，接近51.4%的评分者参考值。这个参考值是把每位评分者跟其他评分者的均值做比较，所以对自动评判系统来说并不是上限。这一上调说明，量表位置可能是造成所观察到的不匹配的原因之一，但它并不是前瞻性的校正，也没有找出根本原因。缺少约定俗成的规范只是若干可能之一，并没有得到证实。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Could confidence help route only Jev’s uncertain cases to a stronger judge and preserve the savings?
segments.zh: 置信度能否帮助系统只把Jev不确定的案例转给更强的评判者，同时保住节省的成本？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: That is the proposed cascade: retain Jev’s confident answers and send less-confident cases to an L-L-M fallback. Confidence can rank Jev’s own correctness, but it does not guarantee correctness. On 6 of 7 graded panels, its area under the receiver operating characteristic curve for identifying its own errors was 0.57 to 0.70; ELLIPSE was the exception at 0.49. Performance also varied by criterion, with values of 0.41 on LFQA factuality and 0.52 on USR PersonaChat engaging.
segments.zh: 这就是他们提出的级联方案：保留Jev有把握的答案，把不太有把握的案例交给大语言模型兜底。置信度可以给Jev自己的正确性排序，但并不能保证正确。在7个评分面板中有6个，它识别自身错误的ROC曲线下面积为0.57到0.70；ELLIPSE是例外，只有0.49。表现也因评分标准而异，在LFQA事实性上为0.41，在USR PersonaChat互动性上为0.52。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: The more surprising issue is whether a fallback can correct a confident mistake. The authors define a repeated error as an L-L-M returning Jev’s same wrong answer on a pair where Jev is wrong. Among 84 sampled high-confidence graded errors, the three L-L-M judges repeated Jev’s error on 242 of 252 verdicts, or 96%. A baseline accounting for criterion and label tendencies predicted 126.7 repeats. The excess supports correlated errors relative to that baseline, though it does not explain why the errors are shared.
segments.zh: 更让人意外的问题是，回退模型到底能不能纠正一个自信的错误。作者把重复错误定义为：在Jev答错的一对问题上，大语言模型给出了和Jev一样的错误答案。在84个采样的高置信度评分错误中，三个大语言模型评判员在252个判定里有242个重复了Jev的错误，也就是96%。一个考虑了评分标准和标签倾向的基线预测会重复126.7次。超出基线的部分说明错误之间存在相关性，但并没有解释这些错误为什么是共享的。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Does that mean all those repeated answers were clearly wrong according to human raters?
segments.zh: 这是否意味着，所有那些重复答案在人类评分者看来都明显是错的？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: No. Many sampled mistakes came from pairs where raters disagreed, so they are not all unambiguous errors against a unanimous human judgment. In a separate HealthBench sample, however, 11 of 12 sampled errors had unanimous physician labels. The cascade results also need careful interpretation: cross-fitted replays of recorded verdicts gained at most 1.5 percentage points on average over the best single judge, and fell below it on 6 panels. Optimistic oracle thresholds gained at most 2 points; these were not newly run live cascades.
segments.zh: 不是。很多被抽出来的错误其实来自评分者意见不一致的样本对，所以它们并不都是违背一致人类判断的明确错误。不过在另一个HealthBench样本里，12个被抽出的错误中有11个得到了医生们一致的标注。级联结果也需要谨慎解读：对已记录判定做交叉拟合重放，相比最好的单一评审平均最多只提升了1.5个百分点，而且在6个评审组上还低于它。乐观的oracle阈值最多也只提升了2个百分点；这些都不是新跑的实时级联。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: How does this connect to the broader work on judge diversity and test-time scaling?
segments.zh: 这与关于评审多样性和测试时扩展的更广泛研究有何联系？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: It extends concerns raised by work such as “Correlated Errors in Large Language Models” into a practical rubric-grading setup: different judges may repeat a cheap judge’s mistakes rather than supply independent corrections. That does not mean diversity is useless in every setting. Here, the measured excess remains after a baseline controls for criterion and label, but it applies to these panels and flash-tier judges. Compared with confidence-escalation approaches, the paper emphasizes that routing helps only when the fallback has useful independent information.
segments.zh: 它把《大语言模型中的相关错误》这类研究提出的担忧，延伸到了一个实际的评分标准打分场景里：不同的评审模型可能会重复一个廉价评审模型的错误，而不是提供独立的纠正。这并不意味着多样性在所有场景下都没用。在这里，即便基线已经控制了评分标准和标签，测得的超额错误依然存在，但它只适用于这些评审组合和flash档位的评审模型。与基于置信度升级的方法相比，这篇论文强调，只有当回退模型能提供有用的独立信息时，路由才有帮助。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: The broader lesson is to evaluate the whole decision pipeline, not just a model’s accuracy or confidence in isolation. Jev’s batching can substantially reduce recorded cost in this setup, especially for binary criteria, while graded performance remains benchmark-dependent. Confidence can help choose which cases to review, but shared mistakes limit what review recovers. Future work should test different prompts, model tiers, and live cascade designs, and investigate rating conventions without assuming they caused the observed gaps. Thanks for listening. If you have any further questions, ask our AI assistant or drop a comment.
segments.zh: 更广泛的启示是，要评估整个决策流程，而不只是孤立地看模型的准确率或置信度。在这个设定下，Jev 的批处理能大幅降低记录成本，尤其是对二元标准而言，但分级表现仍然取决于具体基准。置信度可以帮助选择要复核哪些案例，但共同的错误限制了复核能挽回的东西。未来的工作应该测试不同的提示词、不同层级的模型和实时级联设计，并研究评分惯例，但不要预设它们导致了观察到的差距。感谢收听。如果还有问题，可以问我们的 AI 助手或留言评论。
